recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. The current build already conveys the requested separation, and adding duplicate narrative would not change implementer understanding.
issue_request: FHIR-14289 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core ResearchStudy issue from STU3. It requested updates after condition became a separate element from focus: remove condition from the focus short description, move condition under focus in element order, and update the condition definition away from old BRIDG-style wording. Jira says the change was made and published in the Dec 2017 FHIR ballot.
initial_application: No current git commit explicitly mentions FHIR-14289. The historical ResearchStudy ballot/source trail shows the change family: commit 61b5fa5576 added ResearchStudy.condition in the old spreadsheet source and commit a89b85b64a left focus as 'Drugs, devices, etc. under study' while preserving condition as a separate coded element. Later XML refactors carried that model forward.
additional_context: FHIR-14116 is the directly related Published issue that added condition as its own ResearchStudy semantic instead of leaving it inside focus. Later changes such as FHIR-39083 changed ResearchStudy.focus typing to CodeableReference but did not reverse the condition separation. ResearchStudy remains in the current build scope through source/fhir.ini.
reconciliation: No source change was made. In source/researchstudy/structuredefinition-ResearchStudy.xml, ResearchStudy.focus precedes ResearchStudy.condition; focus has the short 'Drugs, devices, etc. under study'; condition has its own short, definition, CodeableConcept type, condition-code binding, search parameter, and FiveWs mapping exception.

related_jiras.note: Added ResearchStudy.condition as a distinct semantic instead of leaving it inside focus.
Changed ResearchStudy.focus typing to CodeableReference/resource-oriented content without reversing the condition separation.
